topic: General Term of a Binomial Expansion
title: Jump to the 7th Term! General Term Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
(x + 2)^9 has ten long terms, but the question only wants the seventh. Do you really have to write out all ten? In this animated lesson on the binomial theorem (NCERT Chapter 7) a row of lockers shows the one rule that lets you jump straight to any term: the general term.

You will watch a pointer walk along all 11 terms of (a + b)^10 while r counts up, build T(r+1) = nCr a^(n-r) b^r in three small steps, and see why the 7th term uses r = 6, not 7. Then r counts up live to hunt down the constant term of (x + 1/x)^6, a worked example finds the 7th term of (x + 2)^9, the exam trap keeps the minus sign inside b, and an original JEE Main pattern question asks for the term independent of x. A recap card and three questions to check yourself close the lesson.

Note: the general term is not in the current (rationalised) NCERT text, but it is in the JEE Main syllabus.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.
